modified_caption: MC1 scores of model performance on the BBQ task as a function of the number of demonstrations, illustrating comparative accuracy trends. The line plot displays accuracy on the y-axis (ranging from 45 to 55) against the number of demonstrations on the x-axis (0 to 1500). The Squared Exponential model, represented by a dark blue line with circle markers, achieves an initial accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations, rapidly climbing to 56 by 250 demonstrations before stabilizing around 55. The Tanh model, shown in blue, begins at roughly 48 accuracy and exhibits a gradual upward trend, reaching approximately 50 by 1500 demonstrations. The ELU model, depicted in light purple, starts at an accuracy of 46 and remains largely stagnant, with minor fluctuations peaking at 47. The LLaMA-2-chat-7B model, indicated by a dashed magenta line, maintains a consistent accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points. Notably, the Squared Exponential model consistently surpasses all other models, while the ELU model marginally outperforms the Tanh model beyond 1000 demonstrations. The results suggest that the Squared Exponential approach is uniquely effective in leveraging demonstrations to enhance performance on the BBQ task.

modifications.claim: The Tanh model exhibits a gradual upward trend, reaching approximately 50 by 1500 demonstrations.
modifications.reality: The Tanh model remains mostly constant throughout, with no significant upward trend and an accuracy consistently around 48, never reaching 50.

modifications.claim: The ELU model remains largely stagnant, with minor fluctuations peaking at 47.
modifications.reality: The ELU model remains flat at approximately 46 accuracy with no visible fluctuations or peaks at 47.

modifications.claim: The ELU model marginally outperforms the Tanh model beyond 1000 demonstrations.
modifications.reality: The Tanh model consistently outperforms the ELU model at all demonstration points, with no crossover or reversal in ranking.

original_caption: MC1 scores of SEA by using a different number of demonstrations. A higher score indicates a better performance. We find that SEA can start to positively improve the baseline with only 25 demonstrations on both TruthfulQA and BBQ for the 7B LLaMA-2-Chat model.
